prompts.workshop: Use case stylized-concept. Create a new seamless-capable game terrain texture sheet for the user's fantasy dungeon repair workshop, four separate texture sprites. Center of each sprite sits at 25% or 75% in each axis. Upper left: lighter worn grey stone capstone seen vertically above, broad shallow bevels and large stone planes, narrow subtle fine seams, usable as narrow corridor wall edges. Upper right: front-facing vertical dark slate masonry wall face, a carved warm highlight along top, large dark layered stone courses below, no ground, no perspective. Orthogonal, no diagonal tile edges, no isometric diamond. The four original sprites will be clipped and used in a 2D grid game, generate art not a mockup.

EXACT 3 columns x 3 rows on a square true-transparent canvas, all nine axis-aligned square texture swatches of equal width and height with generous transparent gutters. Centers at 1/6, 1/2 and 5/6 on each axis. Keep the swatches opaque from edge to edge, separate, and clear enough to use at about 100 pixels. Painterly stylized game art with chunky shapes, well-defined masonry and tasteful subtle surface wear, no noise or dramatic baked lighting. Warm antique brass, charcoal blue slate, warm taupe flagstones; warm-gold upper highlights and cool deep crevices. Layout is row-major. R1: (1) warm grey square smooth ashlar floor blocks with sparse grout lines, (2) same floor in a medium warm slate tone with staggered larger stones, (3) same floor with one little aged scorch trace and a clean partial fracture.
